audit.why: Packet win rate is 63.64 over 22 games. It is the stored figure and it agrees with the content layer, which has Mel ahead from level 1 through first item.

audit.whatIsWrong: The full layer says HARD, 8/10, and marks all seven phases 'Yasuo'. The content layer says [Mel,Mel,Mel,Mel,Mel,Mel,Yasuo] and the win rate is 63.64.
audit.why: Mel out-ranges Yasuo by 375 units, roots him, and has a global execute; he has no answer until crit items. Calling the whole lane 8/10 HARD contradicts both the stored win rate and the phase text underneath the sides, which describes Mel winning at every stage. The genuine flip is at 2+ items, which the content layer already has right.
audit.corrected: Moved diff to EVEN and difficulty to 6/10, leaving Yasuo's carry threat at 8.5/10 because the late-game half of the read is correct. The seven phases[].side values still read 'Yasuo'; a human needs to set them to [Mel,Mel,Mel,Mel,Mel,Mel,Yasuo].

audit.whatIsWrong: winCon states 'Nothing here works through Wind Wall', tldr says the fight is 'his dash chain vs your snare', and breakdown.cooldowns says Wind Wall 'blocks every projectile'.
audit.why: Golden Eclipse is not a projectile. It carries no projectile flag, and Riot's text has Mel strike everything marked with Overwhelm regardless of distance from her — there is no object travelling from Mel to Yasuo for the wall to intercept. Radiant Volley, Solar Snare and her basic attacks are the projectiles; the ultimate is not. Telling a Mel player that nothing works through Wind Wall makes her hold the single button that does.
audit.corrected: Rebuilt tldr, winCon, phases[3].why, breakdown.cooldowns, dosFull[0] and the Key Ability Interactions block around 'the wall stops Q, E and autos, never the execute'.
sources: champ-data/_kits/mel.json (projectile flag on Q and E only; R flags empty)

audit.whatIsWrong: Last Breath is described as 'R knockup' and 'Last Breath's knockup locks down your frame', as though Yasuo can cast it at will.
audit.why: Last Breath blinks to an Airborne enemy champion — it requires a target that is already knocked up. Mel's kit has no knockup at all, so in a 1v1 Yasuo can only ult off his own 2-stack Steel Tempest whirlwind. That turns his Gathering Storm stack count into a visible ult tell in lane, and it means the real danger in teamfights is an ALLY's knockup, not his own.
audit.corrected: Stated the airborne requirement in spikes[3].text, wants.foe[2], content.late and whys[6], and made the 2-stack tell explicit.
sources: champ-data/_kits/yasuo.json (R Last Breath: blinks to an Airborne enemy champion)

audit.whatIsWrong: Rebuttal is told to 'eat his EQ tornado' without ever saying which cast that is or that it is the only thing worth reflecting.
audit.why: Steel Tempest is Yasuo's only projectile, and only in its whirlwind form at 2 stacks of Gathering Storm — the un-stacked cast is a melee thrust with nothing to send back. That single detail is the difference between holding Rebuttal correctly and burning it on a thrust.
audit.corrected: Named Steel Tempest and the 2-stack whirlwind in wants.you[1], phases[1].why, spikes[2].text and whys[2].
sources: champ-data/_kits/yasuo.json (projectile flag on Q; whirlwind at 2 stacks)

audit.whatIsWrong: Way of the Wanderer is never mentioned.
audit.why: Yasuo builds a shield whenever he is moving, and it triggers on the first champion damage he takes. Against a poke mage that means isolated single bolts of chip are simply absorbed and the Flow bar rebuilds while he walks. Mel has to land damage in bursts for the poke plan to be worth anything, and nothing in the text says so.
audit.corrected: Added the shield to content.early and whys[5] with the practical instruction: two bolts in a row or none.

audit.whatIsWrong: whys[1] says at level 2 'he has no dash value'.
audit.why: Sweeping Blade dashes through any target enemy, and minions count. The moment there is a wave between them Yasuo has dash value, which is exactly when a Mel player following this line will step up and get punished. The correct rule is wave-state dependent, not level dependent.
audit.corrected: Rewrote whys[1] to root him when the wave is thin rather than when it is stacked.
sources: champ-data/_kits/yasuo.json (E Sweeping Blade: dashes through target enemy)

audit.whatIsWrong: breakdown.cooldowns carries no numbers, and tradeBad, dontsFull[2].d and breakdown.trading all claim Rebuttal is 'gone for twenty seconds'.
audit.why: Wind Wall is 25/23/21/19/17 with a 4-second duration — a 21-second window of exposure per cast, which is the single most useful number in the matchup and it was nowhere in the file. Rebuttal is 38/35/33/29/26, so at lane rank it is 38 seconds, not twenty.
audit.corrected: Put Wind Wall's real cooldown and duration into breakdown.cooldowns, dosFull, loading, content.mid and whys[3]; corrected the Rebuttal figure everywhere it appeared.

audit.whatIsWrong: Wave management never connects the wave state to Sweeping Blade.
audit.why: Yasuo's approach is made of minions. A thick wave is a ladder to Mel, a thin one is a wall, and he cannot re-dash the same unit for several seconds. That makes wave state, not cooldowns, the thing that decides whether her 550 range is real.
audit.corrected: Added the wave-as-ladder point to content.early and whys[1].
sources: champ-data/_kits/yasuo.json (E Sweeping Blade: cannot be re-cast on the same enemy for a few seconds)

edits.before: Levels 1-3 are yours because Yasuo has no Windwall value yet and no way to dodge Solar Snare's root. Poke with Q bolts from max range and last-hit safe; the moment he steps up for a CS at level 2, E-root him in place and stack Overwhelm with a second Q. Don't waste E into his minion wave hoping for a dash-cancel — save the orb for when he commits, and respect that his only out early is Flash.
edits.after: Levels 1-3 are yours: Wind Wall has nothing to block yet and Solar Snare is hard to dodge. Poke with Q from max range; when he steps up at level 2, root him and stack Overwhelm with a second Q. Way of the Wanderer shields him whenever he moves, so isolated chip is absorbed — land two bolts in a row or none. Read the wave: Sweeping Blade dashes through minions, so a thick wave is his ladder to you.

edits.before: Levels 4-6 you own the all-in. Your Q ranks up and Overwhelm stacks pile from every trade, so by 6 a single Golden Eclipse can chunk or execute him from range even after he E-dashes onto you. Bait his Windwall — throw a fake Q or step in, and once it's down, root with E and dump real damage. Hold Rebuttal for his EQ tornado: eating it and firing it back denies his poke and his engage tool in one button.
edits.after: Levels 4-6 you own the all-in. Your Q ranks up and Overwhelm stacks pile from every trade, so by 6 a single Golden Eclipse can chunk or execute him from range even after Sweeping Blade lands him on you. Bait Wind Wall — fake a Q or step in — and remember it is 25 seconds at rank 1 but only lasts 4, so one spent wall buys you two clean volleys. Hold Rebuttal for the 2-stack Steel Tempest whirlwind, the only projectile he owns.

edits.before: From 2+ items the lane flips — this is a scaler you cannot out-stat. Once Yasuo has Infinity Edge and Shieldbow he dashes through your minions, Windwall deletes your entire ranged kit, and Last Breath's knockup locks down your dash-less, peel-less frame for a one-combo kill. Win this game before ~25 minutes: snowball your early leads into towers and let your team body him, because your infinitely-scaling passive does not save a squishy who gets jumped.
edits.after: From 2+ items the lane flips — this is a scaler you cannot out-stat. Once Yasuo has Infinity Edge and Shieldbow he dashes through your minions, Wind Wall deletes your entire ranged kit, and Last Breath blinks to anything airborne — in a teamfight every ally knockup is his ticket onto you. Win this game before ~25 minutes: snowball your early leads into towers and let your team body him, because an infinitely-scaling passive does not save a squishy who gets jumped.

notes: BIGGEST FIX HERE: the file told the player 'Nothing here works through Wind Wall'. Golden Eclipse carries no projectile flag and strikes everything marked with Overwhelm regardless of distance, so the wall does not stop it — Radiant Volley, Solar Snare and her basic attacks are the projectiles. That inverts the whole matchup plan and it was stated backwards. PHASE SIDES (needs a human): all seven full.phases[].side values read 'Yasuo' while content.win reads [Mel,Mel,Mel,Mel,Mel,Mel,Yasuo] and the win rate is 63.64. The content layer's chart is the right one. I could not propose the side edits because 'Yasuo' (5) to 'Mel' (3) cannot pass the +/-10% length band. Same fault appears on mel/wukong — worth checking whether every Mel full-layer phase side was generated as the enemy name. SPELLING: the content layer writes 'Windwall' as one word in five places; Riot's name is 'Wind Wall'. I corrected it in the strings I touched.
